title: Particles and density: question set (20 marks)
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Review of Key Stage 3 and working scientifically (9C)
source: Written for science/y9 lesson 53 (Particles and density question set (20 marks) and mark scheme (portal))
intro: Answer every question. Show working and units for calculations. Mark it with the mark scheme.

questions.q: Describe the arrangement and movement of particles in a solid.
questions.a: Close together in a regular pattern (1); vibrate on the spot (1)

questions.q: Describe the arrangement and movement of particles in a gas.
questions.a: Far apart, random (1); move quickly in all directions (1)

questions.q: Name the change of state from liquid to gas, and from gas to liquid.
Explain why a gas can be squashed but a solid cannot.
questions.a: Gas particles have large spaces between them (1); solid particles are touching (1)

questions.q: A block has a mass of 540 g and a volume of 200 cm³. Calculate its density.
Water has a density of 1 g/cm³. Will the block float? Explain.
questions.a: No (1): its density (2.7 g/cm³) is greater than water's (1)

questions.q: A stone pushes the water in a measuring cylinder up from 50 cm³ to 74 cm³. Its mass is 60 g. Find its density.
Explain why ice floats on water.
questions.a: Ice is less dense than liquid water (1) because its particles are held further apart in a pattern (1)

questions.q: Use the particle model to explain diffusion of a smell across a room.
questions.a: Gas particles move randomly (1) and spread from high to low concentration (1)

questions.q: Explain why a balloon in the sun gets bigger.
questions.a: Particles gain energy and move faster (1), hitting the walls harder and more often, so the pressure rises and it expands (1)
